artist.artist_description: Garth Brooks, an American country music singer and songwriter, was born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and raised in Yukon, Oklahoma. He gained fame in the 1990s with hits like "Friends in Low Places" and became one of the best-selling solo albums artists of all time, with over 170 million records sold. Interestingly, Brooks once performed as a stadium rock artist under the alter ego Chris Gaines.

track.detail: This iconic anthem was released in 1990 and quickly became a staple at parties and gatherings. It's a song that celebrates the joy of being with friends, no matter their social standing. The track was penned by Dewayne Blackwell and Earl Bud Lee, inspired by a real-life moment at a songwriters' event. It not only topped the charts but also became a cultural phenomenon, often cited as a symbol of camaraderie and loyalty. The song's success helped solidify its artist's status as a country music legend, influencing countless artists and fans alike. Its enduring popularity is evident in its frequent play at events and its inclusion in various 'best of' lists, showcasing its timeless appeal.

trackranking.intro: Kicking off our list at number 1 in the 1990s country category, 'Friends in Low Places' by Garth Brooks is a must-hear!
